title: AWS Lambda consumer for Amazon MSK via a self-managed Kafka event source with IAM_AUTH (Java)
description: Creates a Lambda function that consumes from an Amazon MSK cluster (IAM auth) declared as a self-managed Kafka event source using the IAM_AUTH auth type; the consumer writes each message to DynamoDB.

introBox.headline: How it works
text: This pattern provisions a self-managed Apache Kafka cluster (3 brokers on 3 EC2 instances, KRaft mode) plus a 4th EC2 instance that acts as a Kafka client and SAM deployment host.

The CloudFormation template creates an Amazon MSK cluster with IAM authentication and a client EC2 instance. The Lambda event source is declared as SELF-MANAGED (not MSK) and pointed at the cluster's IAM bootstrap endpoint (:9098) with the IAM_AUTH auth type.
Authorization is by IAM policy: three IAM roles (admin/producer/consumer) give the interactive clients distinct kafka-cluster permissions, and the Lambda execution role is granted read access.
This deploys via the AWS CLI (deploy_lambda_iam_cli.sh) because AWS SAM does not support the IAM_AUTH self-managed event-source auth type yet. This is an under-development capability.
For detailed deployment instructions see the README.md
